title: C1612 — Camshaft position bank 1 sensor 1 (CMP11)
introduction:
This page gives the camshaft-position connector an address book: the drawing supplies cavity labels, and the assignment table tells you which circuit belongs at each address. I keep the full bank-and-sensor name in view while reading. A familiar plug shape is useful recognition, but it is a lousy substitute for the correct name tag.

Begin with the connector identity table, locate a cavity label in the drawing and follow its matching assignment row across the page. The function descriptions distinguish the camshaft-related connection, signal return and buffered sensor power. Finish with the pigtail records if you need to understand which service parts are listed.

This is a connector-reading reference. Physical viewing direction, gauge convention and the meanings of the Size and Used codes remain undefined here. Preserve those entries without interpreting them as dimensions or test instructions. Physical access, probing, expected electrical results and replacement methods belong to a separate applicable procedure.

edits.why: I use the rounded cavity area and the large rectangular detail on its left as landmarks within the illustration. The cavity labels form a vertical column and increase from top to bottom. That establishes their arrangement on this page, not the viewing side of a connector held in your hand. The identification row beneath the drawing associates it with the recorded shell and harness.

edits.text: Follow each cavity across its circuit row
edits.why: The Cavity entry is the bridge between the drawing and the table. Read across the same row to retain its circuit identifier, color code, gauge, function and terminal part together. Keep the bank-and-sensor description alongside the complete Function wording when using another wiring reference. The labeled signal return and buffered power supply explain different circuit duties; they do not establish a chassis-ground connection or a voltage target for a test.

A pigtail is a connector supplied with attached wire leads. Read each service record as a whole so its service part stays associated with its engineering shell, material and cavity information. The Image column identifies a filename, not another visible drawing. The table provides service-part records without ranking the options or teaching wire selection, splicing, terminal release or installation.
